outcomes.text: Name the muscles, bones and movements at the shoulder and hip joints.
Name the muscles, bones and movements at the elbow, knee, ankle and wrist.
Name the muscles and movements of the trunk and the regions of the vertebral column.
Explain the stretch-shortening cycle and concentric, eccentric and isometric contractions in sporting movements.
Identify agonist, prime mover, antagonist, fixator and synergist roles of a muscle in sport.
Describe the parts of a lever, the three lever classes, and their mechanical advantages and disadvantages.
Apply Newton's three laws of motion to sporting examples.
Explain body stability in terms of centre of mass and its sporting implications.
Calculate force and resultant force, using 1 kg exerting 9.81 N downward.

subtopics.title: Warm-up effects on muscles and bones

outcomes.text: Describe how muscular and skeletal systems respond immediately to warming up and exercise.
Explain how the cardiovascular, circulatory and respiratory systems work alone and together in activity.
Describe the structure and function of the larynx, pharynx, trachea, bronchi, bronchioles and alveoli.
Explain ventilation as a mechanical process, including pressure gradients, partial pressure and diffusion.
Define tidal, reserve and residual volumes and the lung capacities.
Describe the heart's structure, including nodes, valves and chambers, and the blood vessels and blood.
Explain the cardiac cycle, circulation, venous return, vascular shunting, heart rate, stroke volume and cardiac output.
Explain bradycardia, its benefits and how it develops anatomically and physiologically.
Describe how cardiorespiratory and cardiovascular systems respond immediately to warm-up and exercise.
Explain what makes a lifestyle unhealthy and its effects on the cardiovascular and respiratory systems.
Explain the function of the neuro-muscular system during physical activity.
Describe the characteristics of slow twitch, fast oxidative glycolytic and fast glycolytic fibres.
Explain how fibre structure suits each type to different physical activities.
Describe fibre recruitment patterns in endurance and power events and how training affects them.
Describe the parts of the neuro-muscular system, including motor units, actin, myosin, troponin and tropomyosin.
Explain muscle contraction from nerve impulse to response, including sliding filament theory, all-or-none law and wave summation.
Describe how the neuro-muscular system responds immediately to warm-up and exercise.
Describe the chronic adaptations of body systems to training.
Explain the concept of energy in physical activity and sport.
Describe forms of energy, how energy is regenerated, how depletion occurs and recovery.
Name the forms of energy and explain ATP and the use of PC, glycogen and fat to re-make ATP.
Describe the ATP-PC, glycolytic and aerobic energy pathways.
Compare the pathways by speed of ATP production, force supported, intensity, duration and ATP regeneration.
Explain the energy continuum using athletic running events.
Use the continuum to show the joint working of the three pathways.
Place athletic running events on the energy continuum.
Explain fatigue and its causes: energy depletion, dehydration and waste build-up, including the role of lactic acid.
Describe how energy systems respond to warm-up and priming exercise.
Describe the stages of recovery in specific sporting contexts.
Explain the fast component of recovery and phosphagen replenishment.
Explain the slow component of recovery, including lactate removal, the two-hour and 48-hour windows, EIMD and DOMS.
Explain EPOC and the stages of recovery.

units.title: Topic 2: Exercise physiology and applied movement analysis

topics.title: 2.1 Diet and nutrition and their effect on physical activity and performance

outcomes.text: Explain how diet can be manipulated for performance before, during and after activity.
Explain optimal weight for performance, with energy balance, intake and expenditure.
Explain electrolytes and hypotonic, hypertonic and isotonic drinks in hydration.
Describe how supplements can boost energy stores, hydration, recovery and delay fatigue.
Describe contemporary supplements.
Describe strategies for food, fuel and fluid intake, such as carbohydrate loading and protein timing.

topics.title: 2.2 Preparation and training methods in relation to maintaining and improving physical activity and performance

outcomes.text: Explain how preparation and training methods maintain and improve performance.
Describe the fitness tests listed, such as multi-stage, Wingate, Cooper and Yo-Yo tests.
Interpret, calculate and present data from fitness test results.
Explain determinants of running performance for sprint, endurance and intermittent activities.
Define the components of fitness, such as VO2 max, power, agility and flexibility.
Apply the principles of training, including specificity, progressive overload, FITT and reversibility.
Measure and calculate training intensity using %1RM, RPE, target heart rate and work-to-rest ratios.
Use Karvonen's method to find target heart rate.
Describe contemporary technologies used to monitor fitness and performance.
Describe macro, meso and micro cycles and the preparation, competition and transition phases.
Evaluate training methods such as interval, fartlek, plyometrics and PNF, with their advantages and disadvantages.
Describe preparation for performance at altitude, in heat and in humidity.
Describe ways to speed recovery: cool-down, massage, ice baths and compression clothing.

topics.title: 2.3 Injury prevention and the rehabilitation of injury

outcomes.text: Classify common sporting injuries.
Describe acute injuries such as cruciate ligament damage, sprains, fractures and dislocation.
Describe overuse injuries such as shin splints, tendonitis and stress fractures.
Describe injury prevention through conditioning, muscle balance, technique, equipment and risk management.
Describe rehabilitation methods, POLICE and RICE, and weigh their advantages and disadvantages.
Apply definitions, equations and units of linear motion to sport.
Calculate distance, displacement, speed, velocity and acceleration.
Plot, label and interpret distance-time, speed-time and velocity-time graphs.

subtopics.title: Angular motion and moment of inertia

outcomes.text: Explain how angular motion applies in sport.
Explain how mass and its distribution about the axis affect moment of inertia.
Describe the effects of changing moment of inertia when rotating.
Explain conservation of angular momentum in flight and how moment of inertia relates to angular velocity.
Apply projectile motion to refine technique in sport.
Describe the forces in flight: gravity, air resistance and lift.
Explain how release velocity, height and angle determine horizontal displacement.
Explain how technology helps modify technique to improve performance.
Apply aerodynamics and hydrodynamics to sport.
Explain factors affecting fluid friction and air resistance, including streamlining.
Explain lift forces, angle of attack and the Bernoulli effect.
Describe topspin, backspin and sidespin, the Magnus effect, and their effects on flight and bounce.
Explain how fluid mechanics has shaped technique, clothing and equipment advances.
Describe command, reciprocal, guided discovery and problem-solving coaching styles.
Explain how tactics and strategies are developed to optimise competition outcome.
Break a skill into preparation, execution and recovery, and compare it with a higher-level performer.

topics.title: 3.2 The classification and transfer of skills

outcomes.text: Classify skills on gross/fine, paced, discrete/serial/continuous and open/closed continuums.
Describe positive, negative, proactive, retroactive, bilateral and zero transfer.
Explain classical and operant conditioning, reinforcement, punishment and the S-R bond.
Apply Thorndike's laws of effect, exercise and readiness.
Describe Fitts and Posner's stages of learning, coaching needs and feedback at each stage.
Explain how practice methods and structure affect performance.
Describe part, progressive part, whole and whole-part-whole practice, and massed, distributed, fixed and variable practice.
Describe visual, verbal, manual and mechanical guidance, their purpose and effectiveness.
Describe how technology supports guidance to measure, monitor and evaluate performance.
Explain feedback as motivation, reinforcement, and error detection and correction.
Describe positive/negative, KP/KR, concurrent/terminal and intrinsic/extrinsic feedback.
Describe how technology supports feedback.
Describe open and closed loop control models and when each applies.
Describe the information processing models of Welford and Whiting and the DCR phases.
Name the short-term sensory store, short-term memory and long-term memory.
Describe STSS and STM capacity, duration, encoding, chunking and selective attention.
Describe LTM capacity, duration, encoding and recall.
Explain how retrieval and rehearsal link STSS, STM and LTM to output.
Measure and analyse reaction times, using Hick's law and the psychological refractory period.
Explain schema theory, with recall and recognition schema, and its coaching implications.

topics.title: 4.1 Factors that can influence an individual in physical activities

outcomes.text: Explain trait, interactionist and structure-based personality theories in sport.
Explain Wood's triadic model, attitude formation and changing attitudes by cognitive dissonance.
Explain arousal and performance using the inverted-U hypothesis, drive theory and catastrophe theory.
Explain types and dimensions of anxiety, stress, and strategies to manage them.
Distinguish aggression from assertion, with theories, types, causes and reduction strategies.
Explain types and theories of motivation, NACH and NAF, and goal setting.
Explain social facilitation and inhibition, evaluation apprehension, outside influences and strategies to cope.

topics.title: 4.2 Dynamics of a group/team and how they can influence the performance of an individual and/or team

outcomes.text: Explain group cohesion, Carron's and Steiner's models, social loafing, the Ringelmann effect and cohesion strategies.
Apply SMART(ER) targets and the types and time-spans of goals to optimise performance.
Explain Weiner's attribution theory, its dimensions, and attribution retraining.
Explain self-confidence and Vealey's model of sport confidence.
Explain Bandura's self-efficacy, its four sources, and learned helplessness.
Explain leadership styles, their pros and cons, and theories of how leaders emerge.

topics.title: 5.1 The factors leading to the emergence and development of modern day sport

outcomes.text: Describe popular recreations in pre-industrial Britain, for both peasants and aristocracy.
Explain how the Industrial Revolution shaped recreation through industrialisation, urbanisation, education and transport.
Explain the social factors behind rational recreation, including Arnold, athleticism, the sporting press and early governing bodies.
Evaluate teams competing for corporations rather than places.
Explain equality and diversity in disability and gender sport, including ParaSport.
Explain sporting labour migration and its effect on domestic competition and national teams.
Define globalisation of sport, its features and impacts.
Explain how sport spread across the British Empire through the Army, Church, industry and education.
Describe the impact of national and international governing bodies.
Explain the impact of, and issues in bidding for and staging, the Olympics, World Cups and major events.
Explain commercialisation of sport and its impact on society.
Compare advertising, sponsorship, endorsement and merchandising.
Explain broken time payments, spectatorism and media developments in commercialisation.
Explain how the 1968-76 Olympics led to the 1984 Los Angeles commercial blueprint.
Describe franchises, the golden triangle, sports stars as global stars and Americanisation.
Explain ethics, deviance and the pressures to behave deviantly in sport.
Explain how commercialisation affects the sportsmanship ethic and gamesmanship.
Describe forms of deviance, such as doping, simulation, bribery and match fixing.
Describe how governing bodies, governments and the law, with technology, combat deviance.
Explain the role of WADA against performance enhancing drugs.

topics.title: 5.5 The relationship between sport and the media

outcomes.text: Explain the two-way relationship between sport and the media, from print to social media.
Explain technology's impact on viewing, sports media packages and pay per view.

topics.title: 5.6 Development routes from talent identification through to elite performance

outcomes.text: Describe UK talent identification and development, and influences from East Germany and Australia.

topics.title: 5.7 Participation and the health of the nation

outcomes.text: Explain barriers to participation, benefits of mass participation and wearable technology.
Explain mass participation and UK community programmes.
Describe UK participation trends in the 21st century.
